headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: kotaemon can handle API keys and files while transformers has broad shell/filesystem/network access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, and chat transcripts, and transformers can read/write files and run pipelines from local inputs. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from A influence B as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into a shared directory that agent_b parses as prompts or scripts
IF agent_b consumes document text from agent_a without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs by B
Add a manual review step before B processes A-generated files
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document classes, while transformers has broad filesystem read/write and network egress. If they share a workspace, B can read A's sensitive files and potentially transmit them onward. This is a default-dangerous pathway when co-located, with meaningful exfiltration risk.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share any writable filesystem path
IF agent_b is allowed to read files produced or used by agent_a
mitigations: Place A and B in separate workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Restrict B to a read-only input mount
Rotate any API keys exposed to A
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and transformers can write files, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress while kotaemon also uses local files and APIs. Concurrent access to the same workspace can create overwrite and state-corruption conflicts, especially around generated documents or model artifacts. No locking mechanism is documented here, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory tree
IF either agent mutates shared model or document artifacts without locks
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Make shared inputs read-only
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces document-derived answers and citations, and transformers can act as a downstream pipeline component that consumes text or scripts. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into further processing. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but there is no direct evidence of automated action-taking.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification
IF agent_a output is used as the sole source for downstream transformation
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them
Add schema validation on A-to-B handoff
Compare A outputs against source documents
Log and diff intermediate artifacts
requires-engineering: add confidence gating between agents

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and chat transcripts, while transformers can process and persist local files. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations may diverge across the pair. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safest reading is a moderate mismatch risk rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents under different retention policies
IF one agent stores outputs longer than the other
mitigations: Minimize sensitive data in shared workflows
Document retention for each agent
Purge temporary files after each run
Restrict regulated data to one agent
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and logging
